videos.script: Lesson 20 tested the bookshop's API from the outside, in Java. A shop manager cannot read that test. {{java}} Behaviour-driven development starts somewhere else. Before any code exists, three people agree on examples. Five copies in stock. A customer orders two. Three are left. {{examples}} Cucumber keeps examples like these honest. They live in a feature file, as plain sentences. Every sentence is bound to a Java method, so the whole file runs as a test. {{feature}} In this lesson you read Gherkin line by line: given, when, then, a background, and a scenario outline. {{gherkin}} You write the step definitions, and watch a Cucumber expression pull a number and a title out of a sentence. {{steps}} You run the features through JUnit, with Spring and a real database behind them. {{run}} Then you write a sentence nobody has written code for, and read what Cucumber offers you. {{snippet}} And you count what this layer of sentences costs, and decide who it is for. {{cost}}
